sent_to_model:
Would you give me a hand with a post for our family blog, the one Úna set up years ago so the cousins in Boston and Perth and Leeds could keep up with us. I've agreed a sale on the house in Glenmore, the old Mulkerrin place where Tom grew up, and it closes on the 15th of January. Some of the family heard it second-hand before I'd told them properly, which is my own fault, and Declan is very upset with me. I'd rather say it all once, honestly, to everyone, than have it go round in bits on the phone. I want them to understand why, and I want them to know what's being kept. It's not an apology exactly but I'm not going to pretend I handled it well either. Everything I want in it is written out underneath, the hard parts as well. Please don't make me sound like an estate agent or a saint.

- Glenmore house, near Oughterard, built 1931 by Tom's grandfather Pádraig Mulkerrin. Tom died March 2024. I've been driving out every fortnight since, 40 min each way, to air it and check the pipes
- sale agreed 3 November with a young couple, Aoife and Kevin Joyce, he's from Maam Cross, two small children, they want to live in it, not a holiday let
- closes 15 January 2027. Price was fair, under what the Dublin crowd offered in the summer, I took the lower one on purpose
- roof survey in September, Ó Flaithearta's, slates and the back chimney, quote of €38,000, plus the damp in the back bedroom. Septic tank needs replacing to sell to anyone anyway
- keeping the dresser (going to Úna's), Pádraig's fiddle, the photographs, the Sacred Heart lamp, the gate sign. Joyces have said family can come out and walk the land any time
- family day out at the house Sunday 13 December before it's cleared, anyone who can, soup and sandwiches, bring wellies
- Declan heard from his cousin Gráinne on a WhatsApp, not from me. He rang at 2 in the morning his time. Said I was "selling Dad". I said things back I shouldn't have
- Tom proposed to me in the haggard behind that house, 1979, in the rain, with the cattle watching
- the children learning to swim in the lake below the house, Declan refusing to come out until his lips were blue
- last February I slipped on the step at the back door in the frost, lay there twenty minutes before I could get up. Told nobody until now
- Tom always said the house should have children in it, not be a museum
- I regret not consulting Declan, but I am not willing to wait until his summer visit
- I am afraid of being alone at the house since the fall, and I cannot go on maintaining it
- Over the best part of two years I have come to realise that I can keep Tom's memory without keeping the house
- tell them the date it closes so nobody hears it from someone else again
- say sorry for how they found out, not for the decision
- Declan reads these. I want him to know I'm not angry and the door is open
- invite everyone to the day out in December

(About me: retired primary-school teacher, 71, Galway, Ireland. Length: it should come to roughly 2,000-4,000 words.)

must_cover: Explains the supplied upkeep costs, travel, repair needs, fall and fear of being alone; gives the agreed sale and closing dates.
Explains choosing the Joyces’ lower fair offer for a family home over a holiday let, Tom’s wish for children there, and the buyers’ offer of continued family walks.
Recounts the supplied house history, proposal and swimming memories, the gradual recognition that keeping Tom’s memory does not require ownership, and what is being kept.

Recounts Gráinne’s WhatsApp and Declan’s 2am selling-Dad accusation; regrets her response and not consulting him, apologises for second-hand news, stands by selling and explains refusing to wait until summer.
Invites everyone before clearance on Sunday 13 December for soup and sandwiches with wellies, and tells Declan she is not angry and is open to talking.
Identifies the buyers as Aoife and Kevin Joyce, says Kevin is from Maam Cross and they have two small children.
Discloses that she told nobody about the February fall until this post.
must_not_reveal: An apology for the decision to sell the house.
